span.label: RETRACTED (A CORRELATION COEFFICIENT UNDER A CAUSAL EDGE) · rlPFC —causes→ confidence
span.note: RETRACTED: A CORRELATION COEFFICIENT UNDER A CAUSAL EDGE. The whole span: 'Indeed, in right rostrolateral PFC we found a SIGNIFICANT NEGATIVE CORRELATION between the confidence beta and A roc (r = -0.47, p = 0.025), which remained after controlling for Report trial type.' A reported r and p, with a control - careful correlational reporting - recorded as `rlPFC --causes--> confidence`. Sister case to Fleming2010[4], retracted earlier tonight, where the same group wrote out the disclaimer explicitly: 'we cannot establish whether the covariation ... reflects a causal role'. — strength of the relation: 0.7 — correlational; negative beta, and the strength of the relation predicts metacognitive ability across people
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: rlPFC —distinct-from→ dACC
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER CONFIDENCE-RELATED ACTIVITY PREDICTS METACOGNITIVE ABILITY. 'Quotation withheld.' All these regions TRACK confidence; only one predicts how good the metacognition is. Tracking and predicting are different tests and the regions separate on the second, not the first. Q-467. · strength of the relation: 0.9 — both track confidence; only rlPFC predicts metacognitive ability, which is the paper's third criterion doing the separating
